advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_current_impact_model_version()` fail loudly (raise/exit) instead of returning a hardcoded `"code-v5"` when neither the import nor the source-file read yields a version.
evidence: `m = re.search(...); if m: return m.group(1); return "code-v5"`
docstring: "A hardcoded default is how this script silently kept analysing a retired cohort: the model moved to code-v5 while the default still said code-v3"
The fallback cannot distinguish 'read the real version' from 'defaulted to a guess that may be stale' — the caller receives an authoritative-looking version string either way.
advisory.finding: `_current_impact_model_version()`'s two error branches (sidecar.py unreadable, or the regex failing to match) return a HARDCODED literal `"code-v5"`, which silently re-introduces exactly the stale-hardcoded-default failure the function's own docstring condemns: when the model advances past code-v5 and this fallback path is taken, the script analyses a retired cohort and (per ADR 0036, no pooling) produces an empty-but-plausible segment rather than an error.
scenarios: Run in a checkout where `rebar` is not importable and `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` is absent/moved (OSError) or IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION is defined differently than the anchored regex expects.
The production model advances to code-v6 while this literal still says code-v5.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the two `return "code-v5"` fallbacks with a `raise SystemExit(...)` (or sentinel that main() rejects) so an unresolvable model version is an error, not a plausible-looking guess.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Thread `--repo-root` into `_normalize_criterion` so `registry.normalize_criteria([label], repo_root)` uses the same vocabulary as `_load_routing`.
evidence: registry.normalize_criteria signature: `def normalize_criteria(criteria, repo_root=None)` and its body `known = set(effective_criteria(repo_root))`
`ROUTING = _load_routing(args.repo_root)` at main() line 367 — routing honours --repo-root but normalization does not
advisory.finding: `_normalize_criterion()` calls `registry.normalize_criteria([label])` with no `repo_root`, so synonym/label normalization uses the ambient default (cwd) vocabulary, whereas `_load_routing(args.repo_root)` reads routing from the `--repo-root` overlay. Under a project overlay reached only via `--repo-root`, the two can disagree — a project criterion recognised for routing may not be recognised as 'known' during normalization (and vice-versa), pooling labels inconsistently with the routing table the same run reports against.
scenarios: Running the generator with `--repo-root` pointed at a checkout other than cwd that carries a project `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` adding project criteria.
advisory.suggested_fix: Pass the repo root through to `_normalize_criterion` (e.g. store it in a module global alongside ROUTING/SYNONYMS) and call `registry.normalize_criteria([label], repo_root)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a newly_blocking test for an advisory/UNROUTED criterion to cover the `float('inf')` ceiling branch.
evidence: `cur_thr, cur_blocking, _ = posture_of(criterion)` then `ceiling = cur_thr if cur_blocking else float("inf")` (calibrate_code_review_thresholds.py:290-291)

Test drives only `sec`->`security` which routes blocking@0.54: `assert criterion == "security"` and `assert [f["priority"] for f in findings] == [0.45]` (tests/unit/test_code_review_criteria_routing.py:290-292)
ABSENCE: no test constructs an advisory/unrouted criterion to exercise the `float('inf')` ceiling of newly_blocking
advisory.finding: newly_blocking's ceiling branch for an advisory/UNROUTED criterion (`ceiling = cur_thr if cur_blocking else float("inf")`) is untested; the only test (test_newly_blocking_uses_normalized_dump_specs) drives `security`, which is routed blocking@0.54, so only the `cur_blocking` branch is exercised. A finding tagged with an advisory criterion at priority above its 0.95 default (e.g. criterion `concurrency` advisory, finding priority 0.96 with thr=0.52) exercises the `float('inf')` ceiling and is never checked.
scenarios: Dumping newly-blocking findings for an advisory criterion (e.g. concurrency@0.52) where a finding sits above the 0.95 default

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extract classify()/exec-dispatch to a module-level function and add a test that a routed synonym is not DET/ATTEST while an exec==DET row is.
evidence: Added branch `if r["exec"] == "DET": return ("DET/ATTEST", ...)` and the fallback `if r["exec"] == "-" and r["p_block"] > 0 and (r["mv"] is None or mv < 0.05): ...` (calibrate_code_review_thresholds.py:514-519)
Commit message: "DET criteria are identified by their routing `exec` rather than a ... heuristic that misfired on `sec`"
ABSENCE: no test in tests/unit/test_code_review_criteria_routing.py invokes or asserts the DET/ATTEST classification outcome
advisory.finding: The headline classification fix — DET/attestation criteria identified by routing `exec == "DET"` instead of the old `p_block>0 and validity~0` heuristic that misfired on the `sec` synonym — has no test exercising classify(). The synonym-pooling half (_crits) is tested, but the resulting reclassification (that a routed synonym like `sec`->`security` no longer lands in DET/ATTEST, and that a true `exec==DET` row still does) is unverified.
scenarios: A row with exec=DET must classify DET/ATTEST; a routed synonym row (formerly misfiring) must NOT
